# Connecting

  <ComparisonRow label="Set up">
    <ComparisonCell choice="mcp">Instant to 15 minutes</ComparisonCell>
    <ComparisonCell choice="cli">Instant</ComparisonCell>
    <ComparisonCell choice="api">Hours to days</ComparisonCell>
  </ComparisonRow>
  <ComparisonRow label="How it runs">
    <ComparisonCell choice="mcp">
      Inside a conversational assistant
    </ComparisonCell>
    <ComparisonCell choice="cli">
      In a terminal, local agent, script, or CI
    </ComparisonCell>
    <ComparisonCell choice="api">
      In deterministic code
    </ComparisonCell>
  </ComparisonRow>
  <ComparisonRow label="Permission and Attribution">
    <ComparisonCell choice="mcp">
      Actions are attributed to the acting user or agent. The agent acts as the
      Ramp user who authenticated the connection. Permissions do not exceed the
      user or agent's role.
    </ComparisonCell>
    <ComparisonCell choice="cli">
      Actions are attributed to the acting user or agent. The agent acts as the
      Ramp user who authenticated the connection. Permissions do not exceed the
      user or agent's role.
    </ComparisonCell>
    <ComparisonCell choice="api">
      Access is limited to the scopes granted to your app.
    </ComparisonCell>
  </ComparisonRow>
  <ComparisonRow label="Strengths">
    <ComparisonCell choice="mcp">
      Easy setup, already available in some cases, and instant with Claude chat
      or an out-of-the-box connector
    </ComparisonCell>
    <ComparisonCell choice="cli">
      Structured output, broad workflows, and easy local automation
    </ComparisonCell>
    <ComparisonCell choice="api">
      Maximum control over interfaces, workflows, and backend logic
    </ComparisonCell>
  </ComparisonRow>
  <ComparisonRow label="Weaknesses">
    <ComparisonCell choice="mcp">
      Slower performance
    </ComparisonCell>
    <ComparisonCell choice="cli">
      Requires installation and access to a coding agent or terminal
    </ComparisonCell>
    <ComparisonCell choice="api">
      Requires the most engineering, security, and lifecycle ownership
    </ComparisonCell>
  </ComparisonRow>
</ComparisonTable>

Use the [Ramp app](https://app.ramp.com) when a person needs to review context,
handle an exception, or complete work directly. The
[Agent Tools reference](/docs/reference/agent-tools) lists every tool available
in the CLI and MCP.

## CLI

Use the CLI when the agent has terminal access, needs structured output, or
should follow a repeatable skill. The CLI works well in Claude Code, Codex,
Cursor, scripts, and CI.

<CliInstallButton />

### Coding agents

```bash
# Claude Code
claude mcp add --transport http ramp https://mcp.ramp.com/mcp

# Codex
codex mcp add ramp --url https://mcp.ramp.com/mcp
```

Coding agents can also use the [CLI](#cli).

## What the connection can do

The connection acts as the Ramp user who authorized it and never exceeds that
user's permissions. On the consent screen, the user chooses **Full access** or
**Read-only**. Connections expire after 30 days; reconnect to renew. Admins
control who can connect with the **Manage connections to Ramp via MCP, CLI and
other AI connectors** role permission and can revoke connections; revoking one
cuts off every AI tool that shares it. See
[Manage connected AI tools](https://support.ramp.com/managing-connected-ai-tools).

## Developer API

Use the API when your product owns the interface and backend workflow. Your
team is responsible for OAuth, scopes, webhooks, retries, and the customer
experience.

[View API reference](https://docs.ramp.com/developer-api/v1)

## Custom MCP clients

Point the client at `https://mcp.ramp.com/mcp`. For the Ramp sandbox
(demo.ramp.com, the same environment as the CLI's `--env sandbox`), use
`https://demo-mcp.ramp.com/mcp`. Clients that read MCP JSON usually expect:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ramp": {
      "url": "https://mcp.ramp.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Custom clients and gateways need their exact redirect URI allowlisted before
authorization can complete:

- Use `https://`, or `http://` only with `localhost` or `127.0.0.1`. Ramp also
  accepts the `claude://`, `cursor://`, `grokbot://`, and `perplexity-app://`
  schemes; other custom schemes are not supported.
- Submit the exact host. Wildcard subdomains are not supported.
- [Request redirect URI access](https://docs.ramp.com/developer-api/v1/mcp-redirect-whitelist-request)
  for the client or gateway.

## Troubleshooting

### Authentication stops working

Connections expire after 30 days. Disconnect and reconnect Ramp in the client to
renew. If a custom client keeps stale credentials, clear its cached MCP auth.

### Write tools are missing

The connection may be read-only. Reconnect and choose **Full access**, and
check that the user's Ramp role allows the action.

### The CLI keeps logging out

CLI sessions stay signed in while they are used and refresh on each use. After
a period of inactivity, run `ramp auth login` again. If it happens sooner,
confirm that the runtime preserves `~/.config/ramp/config.toml`; ephemeral
coding environments may replace that file between sessions.

### A query returns too much data

Reporting queries return up to 1,000 rows per page. Narrow the date range or
filters, or ask the agent to page through the results.

### Unsupported redirect URI

See [Custom MCP clients](#custom-mcp-clients) to submit the exact URI.

### A receipt attachment does not reach MCP

Chat attachments are not forwarded to Ramp MCP. Ask the agent for a receipt
upload link, or use the Ramp CLI or Ramp app.
